claims.text: Annual (well-child visit) — Behind schedule: if a child comes under care for the first time at any point, or items weren't done at the suggested age, bring the schedule up to date as soon as possible.
claims.quote: 1. If a child comes under care for the first time at any point on the schedule, or if any items are not accomplished at the suggested age, the schedule should be brought up to date at the earliest possible time.

claims.text: Annual (well-child visit) — Exam: an age-appropriate physical exam at each visit, with the infant totally unclothed and older children undressed and suitably draped.
claims.quote: At each visit, age-appropriate physical examination is essential, with infant totally unclothed and older children undressed and suitably draped.

claims.text: Annual (well-child visit) — Adolescents: screen for depression and suicide risk, making every effort to preserve the adolescent's confidentiality.
claims.quote: Screen adolescents for depression and suicide risk, making every effort to preserve confidentiality of the adolescent.

claims.text: Annual (well-child visit) — Substance use: a recommended tool to assess alcohol, tobacco and nicotine, marijuana and other substance use (including opioids) is CRAFFT (crafft.org).
claims.quote: A recommended tool to assess use of alcohol, tobacco and nicotine, marijuana, and other substances, including opioids is available at http://crafft.org.

claims.text: Intake (prenatal and newborn visits) — Prenatal visit: recommended for high-risk parents, first-time parents and those who ask; include anticipatory guidance, pertinent medical history, and the benefits of breastfeeding and planned feeding method.
claims.quote: 2. A prenatal visit is recommended for parents who are at high risk, for first-time parents, and for those who request a conference. The prenatal visit should include anticipatory guidance, pertinent medical history, and a discussion of benefits of breastfeeding and planned method of feeding

claims.text: Intake (prenatal and newborn visits) — Newborn follow-up: evaluate newborns within 3 to 5 days of birth and within 48 to 72 hours after hospital discharge, including feeding and jaundice.
claims.quote: Newborns should have an evaluation within 3 to 5 days of birth and within 48 to 72 hours after discharge from the hospital to include evaluation for feeding and jaundice.

claims.text: H&P (sick visit) — Independent historian: someone (eg, a parent or guardian) who gives a history in addition to the patient's, because the patient can't give a complete or reliable one (eg, developmental stage) or a confirmatory history is needed. Translation services don't count.
claims.quote: Independent historian(s): An individual (eg, parent, guardian, surrogate, spouse, witness) who provides a history in addition to a history provided by the patient who is unable to provide a complete or reliable history (eg, due to developmental stage, dementia, or psychosis) or because a confirmatory history is judged to be necessary. In the case where there may be conflict or poor communication between multiple historians and more than one historian is needed, the independent historian requirement is met. It does not include translation services.

claims.text: Progress — Progress: document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and any revision of the diagnosis.
claims.quote: You should document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and revision of diagnosis
